name: MITRE Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems (ATLAS)
disclaimer: Academic reference and mapping crosswalk inspired by MITRE ATLAS matrices and techniques. Not officially endorsed or certified by MITRE.

controls.title: LLM Prompt Injection (Direct & Indirect)
controls.description: Adversaries craft inputs or insert malicious instructions into external content ingested by an LLM application to override instructions and hijack execution.
controls.verification_guidance: Check for prompt structure sanitization, context boundary isolation, and secondary confirmation on high-risk tools.

controls.title: LLM Jailbreak
controls.description: Adversaries use roleplay, hypothetical framing, cipher encoding, or adversarial suffix tokens to bypass AI safety guardrails and system restrictions.
controls.verification_guidance: Verify multi-layer defensive guardrails (input classifier + output classifier) and adversarial test coverage.

controls.title: Data Poisoning
controls.description: Adversaries manipulate RAG knowledge sources or training datasets to introduce malicious associations or backdoors.
controls.verification_guidance: Verify cryptographic hashing of ingested knowledge chunks, origin verification, and anomaly detection in vector search spaces.

controls.title: Exfiltration via ML Inference
controls.description: Adversaries extract sensitive model weights, training data, or proprietary system prompt instructions by querying the model repeatedly.
controls.verification_guidance: Audit rate-limiting on inference endpoints, differential privacy safeguards, and prompt leak filters.

controls.title: ML Supply Chain Compromise
controls.description: Adversaries compromise upstream third-party models, packages (PyPI, npm), or checkpoints loaded from public hubs.
controls.verification_guidance: Inspect package lockfiles, model weight signatures, vulnerability scanning on AI libraries, and safe unpicklers.
